analysis.title: GS Korea Final: KOSPI Advances on Foreign Buying (11 Nov 2026)
key_insights: KOSPI reclaimed its 5,300 handle into noon on foreign bids centered in Tech (+$480m). Turnover was -16% vs 20-day averages and the desk would not call the move conviction-driven.

Memory led, with SK Hynix (+5.4%) outperforming Samsung Electronics (+3.6%). The desk reads this as a possible gradual return to risk. The gains also looked squeezy, especially in semis equipment and EV names (GS Korea Top Shorted basket GSKRTPDT +2.1%).
Desk flows were more benign, with a good mix of long-only and hedge fund bids in memory. Samsung and Hynix trading volumes lagged recent averages by -16% and -18%.
Foreign investors bought +$403m of Samsung Electronics and +$98m of SK Hynix. The two-day memory gains came despite SOX -0.4% and NVDA -5.5% overnight.
Reported headline: Tesla plans to adopt HBM for its next-generation Dojo D3 AI chip, a potential new demand source for Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron.

Korea insurance index (KRXINS) fell -2.0%. Cited reasons are falling long-term KTB yields, expected weak 3Q earnings (due mostly tomorrow) on mark-to-market losses in alternative investments, and reports of a proposed KDIC deposit insurance premium hike.

Samsung Fire & Marine (000810) fell -5.5%. GS Investment Research says the Canopius acquisition fits management's stated aim of investing in higher-return entities and is fully funded from existing capital.

ISU Petasys (007660) rose +19.4%, tied to news that Google is introducing new TPU variants. The company supplies ultra-high-layer PCBs/MLBs for Google's custom ASIC TPUs. Local institutions bought +$21m net while foreigners sold -$19m.

market_movers.rationale: Samsung Electronics (005930) +3.6% with FII buying of +$403m. The Tesla Dojo D3 HBM report is a potential demand source. Volume was -16% vs recent averages.
SK Hynix (000660) +5.4% with FII buying of +$98m. It outperformed Samsung. Volume was -18% vs recent averages.
Samsung Fire & Marine (000810) -5.5% in a weak insurance sector. GS maintains the Canopius deal is consistent with management's strategy and fully funded from existing capital.
ISU Petasys (007660) +19.4% on Google TPU variant news. It supplies high-layer PCBs for Google's custom ASIC TPUs. The move was local institution driven.

earnings_insights: Korea insurance 3Q earnings, mostly due 11/12, are said to be very weak because of deteriorating investment profits (mark-to-market on alternative investments). This is a market-talk expectation, not a reported figure.

macro_indicators.interpretation: KRW strengthened alongside foreign equity buying.
The index reclaimed the 5,300 level on foreign buying, but turnover was -16% vs the 20-day average.

risk_factors: The rally looks squeeze-driven with below-average volumes, so it may not hold.
NVDA -5.5% and SOX -0.4% overnight weigh on the semis backdrop.
Weak Korea insurance 3Q earnings, falling long-term KTB yields and a possible KDIC premium increase pressure the insurance sector.
vol_and_positioning: Squeeze-type gains in the most-shorted Korean names: GS Korea Top Shorted basket (GSKRTPDT) +2.1%, concentrated in semis equipment and EV.
Memory demand from long-only and hedge fund clients was mixed, but the desk said it is hard to call it conviction-driven. Index activity lagged, with turnover -16% vs the 20-day average.
